articles.title: In 2015, Queensland began turning end-of-life tyres into road material; over the next decade 2.4 million tyres were kept out of landfill as crumb rubber was blended into asphalt and road seals
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Australia has been looking for better ways to deal with the growing mountain of tyres discarded after heavy use for years. Now Queensland’s Sunshine C.
articles.body: Australia has been looking for better ways to deal with the growing mountain of tyres discarded after heavy use for years. Now Queensland’s Sunshine Coast is testing whether one of the toughest types of tyres can find a second life under motorists’ wheels, states a 2024 report by the Department of Transport and Main Roads, Queensland Government. It has been reported that the Sunshine Coast Council used crumb rubber from end-of-life off-the-road (OTR) tyres in asphalt and road-sealing works along Railroad Parade in Glass House Mountains, Spalls Road in Diddillibah and Perlan Street in Nambour. The 2024 report states that the trial featured OTR tyres with a proven track record in Queensland’s mining and agricultural industries. They recycled their rubber into road material, a potential homegrown solution to a waste stream that’s long been a challenge to manage. Scroll down to read the details.From heavy industry to local roadsFor the uninitiated, OTR tyres are built to withstand harsh environments and are used in industries such as mining, agriculture and quarrying. However, at the end of their working lives, it can be difficult to find productive uses for the large volumes of rubber they contain. The Sunshine Coast project looked into whether that material can instead be used in a circular economy where tyres used by regional industries are processed into crumb rubber and then incorporated into local infrastructure. The project was a collaboration between Sunshine Coast Council, Boral and its subsidiary Allens Asphalt, Carroll Engineering and Puma Energy Bitumen. The project was led by the Australian Flexible Pavement Association, with support from RMIT University and Tyre Stewardship Australia, adds the report.Rubber testing in the right mixThe trial was intended to determine the best combination of rubber binder and asphalt for roads with different traffic levels. For example, the asphalt mix at the Perlan Road test site in Nambour was 1.7% rubber by total mass. Researchers tested the different mixes over time to test their durability and how they will work with local road conditions. The technical assessment involved accelerated aging tests performed by RMIT. The project also studed the environmental and economic benefits of using recycled OTR rubber in road construction.Facing a major challenge in tyre wasteTyre Stewardship Australia estimated that around 245,000 tons of OTR rubber products are produced each year in Australia. Much of this material was disposed of in situ or through low-value or unrecovered pathways. That leads to potential environmental and health issues, and also was a lost economic opportunity. Using the material in roads could help divert more tyres from disposal and create a demand for recycled rubber. The approach also could generate local jobs, business opportunities and regional economic activity.A model for other regions to emulateThe Sunshine Coast trial could have far-reaching implications beyond the roads being tested out now. If the recycled rubber asphalt was a success the findings could provide councils in mining, agricultural and other OTR tyre using areas with practical information to develop similar local recycling programs. The project was also designed to show how regional industries can create a local market for materials that otherwise had limited end-of-life options.Building the roads of tomorrowThe trial was part of a broader push to make Australian infrastructure more sustainable, safe and high performing. The project was part of the Sunshine Coast Council’s desire to be Australia’s most sustainable region. It provided a potential means of keeping valuable rubber in use for tyre users and recycling industries. The final results were expected to provide technical and environmental data including life-cycle assessments that could help other councils to decide whether OTR tyre-derived road materials were appropriate for use in their own communities. A road trial on three Sunshine Coast streets that began eventually provided a blueprint to turn one of Australia’s trickiest industrial waste streams into a useful ingredient for the roads of the future.Images Courtesy: istock and Tyre Stewardship AustraliaCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Minnesota mother escaped a burning home, realised her toddler was still inside and went back; firefighters found her shielding the child with her body
articles.summary: US News: A 38-year-old Minnesota mother died after returning to a burning St. Paul home to rescue her 3-year-old daughter; firefighters later found her shieldi.
articles.body: A 38-year-old Minnesota mother died after returning to a burning St. Paul home to rescue her 3-year-old daughter; firefighters later found her shielding the child with her own body. Bonnie Pierce was inside a duplex on the 700 block of Magnolia Avenue East on August 22 with two of her daughters, Aurora and Grace, when the fire broke out. According to a GoFundMe organised for Pierce’s family, her 12-year-old daughter Aurora managed to escape by pushing out an air-conditioning unit and climbing through a window. Pierce also initially made it out of the house. But after realising that her youngest daughter, Grace, was still inside, she went back into the burning home. St. Paul firefighters subsequently found Pierce and the toddler in a bedroom amid heavy fire, thick black smoke and extreme heat. Pierce was unresponsive and suffered severe injuries. She died on August 24, while Grace remained hospitalised in critical condition and was expected to make a full recovery, according to the family fundraiser.Fire breaks out in St. PaulThe incident happened on the afternoon of August 22 at a duplex in the 700 block of Magnolia Avenue East in St. Paul, Minnesota. According to the St. Paul Fire Department, crews arrived to find heavy fire conditions, thick black smoke and extreme heat inside the home. Firefighters immediately began searching the property for people who might still be trapped. During the search, a firefighter located an adult woman in a bedroom. As he lifted her in an attempt to remove her from the house, he discovered that a toddler was underneath her. Another firefighter was called to help, and the two firefighters carried both victims outside. The woman was later identified as Bonnie Lynn Pierce, while the toddler was identified as her daughter, Grace.Officials said Pierce and Grace were both taken to the hospital. Pierce died two days after the fire, on August 24, as a result of her injuries. Grace remained in hospital in critical condition following the incident. The fire department has not publicly determined or announced the cause of the fire. Interim St. Paul Fire Chief Greg Duren said the investigation remained open during the department's August 29 media briefing.Pierce went back for GraceThe circumstances surrounding Pierce's return to the burning home are described in greater detail in the family’s GoFundMe campaign. According to the fundraiser, Pierce was inside the house with Aurora and Grace when the fire began. Aurora escaped by kicking out an air-conditioning unit and climbing through a window. Pierce also managed to get outside initially. However, she then realised that Grace was still inside. Pierce decided to return to the burning home to find her youngest daughter. Firefighters later found the mother and child together inside the bedroom, with Pierce positioned over Grace.As per the family's fundraiser, Pierce was found unresponsive and firefighters immediately began CPR. It also states that she had been without oxygen for approximately 15 minutes and suffered burns covering 48% of her body. Despite efforts by first responders and medical personnel, Pierce died from her injuries on August 24. The St. Paul Fire Department confirmed the central detail of the rescue: firefighters found Pierce shielding the toddler beneath her as they searched the smoke-filled home. Chief Duren described the circumstances as demonstrating an extraordinary depth of love and sacrifice, while emphasising that the family was grieving.Family faces devastating lossPierce's death has left her four daughters and grandson facing the aftermath of the tragedy. The family fundraiser identifies her daughters as Alaynah, Aurora, Jemma and Grace, and her grandson as Atlas. The GoFundMe was established to support the family following Pierce’s death and to help with Grace’s continuing medical and recovery needs, immediate living expenses and other unexpected costs resulting from the fire. Grace survived the incident and is expected to make a full recovery.The family has remembered Pierce not only for the circumstances of her death but also for the person she was in life. At the fire department's August 29 briefing, her sister Jenny McGovern described her as someone who died saving her daughter. Family members remembered Pierce as funny, vivacious and “wacky.” For the family, the tragedy has brought both an immense loss and hope for Grace's recovery. Pierce ultimately died from her injuries two days later, but firefighters' discovery of her body over her daughter underscored the lengths she went to protect her child. The investigation into the Magnolia Avenue fire remains ongoing, and authorities have not announced what caused the blaze.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Zealand opens five marine reserves with groundbreaking Maori co-management model to protect Otago’s coastal ecosystems
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Along New Zealand’s Otago coast, a new approach to marine conservation is putting Indigenous knowledge and government authority side by side. On July .
articles.body: Along New Zealand’s Otago coast, a new approach to marine conservation is putting Indigenous knowledge and government authority side by side. On July 1, 2026, five new marine reserves came into force across 308 square kilometres of coastal waters, creating the country’s first group of marine reserves to be jointly managed by Māori and the government. The network, known as Te Au Roa o Te Rakihouia, was developed through more than a decade of work involving Kāi Tahu and government agencies. The reserves provide full no-take protection for important marine habitats, including rocky reefs, kelp forests, seabed environments and offshore canyons. What makes the initiative particularly significant is its governance model: Kāi Tahu and New Zealand’s Department of Conservation share decision-making responsibilities and work alongside a joint marine ranger team. As reported by Ocean Economist, the model represents a different way of approaching marine protection, combining formal conservation systems with Indigenous stewardship and local knowledge.Five new marine reserves now protect 308 square kilometres of Otago coastlineThe five reserves form a new protected network along Otago’s southeastern coast and came into force after being gazetted on May 28, 2026. Together, they cover 308 square kilometres of coastal marine habitat and provide full no-take protection, meaning activities such as fishing and other forms of extraction are prohibited within the reserves. The protected areas include a range of underwater environments that support marine species and coastal ecosystems, from rocky reefs and kelp forests to seabed habitats and offshore canyons. The creation of the network is particularly notable because New Zealand had gone more than a decade without establishing a new group of marine reserves. The reserves are intended not simply to draw lines on a map but to give vulnerable marine ecosystems areas where natural processes can continue with fewer pressures from human activity.Kāi Tahu and the government will share responsibility for the watersThe most distinctive part of the initiative is what happens after the protected areas are established. Rather than leaving management entirely to a government conservation agency, the reserves are jointly managed by Kāi Tahu and New Zealand’s Department of Conservation. The arrangement brings Indigenous and government authority into a shared decision-making framework. The model also includes a joint marine ranger team, giving the partnership a practical presence on the water rather than limiting collaboration to policy discussions. The approach reflects the role of Māori communities as long-standing guardians of their coastal environments, while bringing that knowledge together with the statutory responsibilities and resources of the Department of Conservation. Ocean Economist described the arrangement as an innovative governance model, highlighting how the two parties will work together to manage the reserves.The marine network could reshape how New Zealand protects its coastal ecosystemsThe Otago reserves arrive at a time when marine ecosystems face growing pressure from human activity and climate-related changes. Protecting areas from extraction can give fish, seabed communities and kelp ecosystems greater opportunity to recover, while creating protected spaces where ecological processes can continue with less disturbance. The initiative also carries significance beyond the five reserves themselves. Its shared-management structure could provide a model for future conservation projects where Indigenous communities have an established relationship with the environment being protected. New Zealand’s Department of Conservation has already described marine protection elsewhere as a way to support tangata whenua in their roles as kaitiaki, or guardians, of marine environments. For Otago, the immediate goal is healthier protected waters. But the longer-term experiment is equally important: whether conservation can become more effective when those responsible for protecting ecosystems also share authority over how that protection is carried out.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday after Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly.This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the state cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the cabinet of the TVK government? Because the TVK minister's statements are a scathing vote of no confidence, and TVK is an alliance partner, but the Congress party still continues to be in the TVK government. Why is the Congress party not withdrawing support to the TVK government after their leader Rahul Gandhi has been insulted?" news agency ANI quoted Kesavan saying.The issue has gained further attention after a private media survey placed Vijay among the preferred candidates for PM in 2029, behind PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi.The TVK government was formed after the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, when the party emerged as the largest force and formed the government with support from VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI and CPI(M).Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Just 41-46ft: Airlink jets’ dangerously low flypast over Cape Town stadium - Watch
articles.summary: Rest of World News: An Airlink Embraer jet flew an estimated 41 to 46 feet (12.5 to 14 metres) above the roof of Cape Town's DHL Stadium during a pre-match formation flyp.
articles.body: An Airlink Embraer jet flew an estimated 41 to 46 feet (12.5 to 14 metres) above the roof of Cape Town's DHL Stadium during a pre-match formation flypast, according to Flightradar24 data, as South Africa's aviation regulator reviews the manoeuvre.The two Airlink jets flew over the stadium on Saturday, shortly before South Africa faced New Zealand in the second Test of their four-match rugby series. Footage of the flypast quickly spread online, with some angles making the lead aircraft appear to pass extremely close to the stadium roof as pyrotechnics were set off nearby.Airlink said the flypast had been planned and rehearsed with “guidance, approval and support” from the South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) and Air Traffic Navigation Services.The airline has also voluntarily provided flight data from both aircraft to SACAA for an independent assessment of whether the manoeuvre complied with its authorised parameters.Tracking data puts clearance below 50 feetFlightradar24 initially showed a 50-foot altitude reading, but clarified that this was based on pressure altitude rather than the aircraft's actual clearance above the stadium.After adjusting for atmospheric pressure in Cape Town, the tracking service estimated that the lead aircraft was flying at 205 to 210 feet above mean sea level. With the stadium estimated to stand about 164 feet high, the aircraft's clearance was calculated at approximately 41 to 46 feet.Flightradar24 cautioned that the figure was an estimate and carried a margin of error.Videos of the flypast generated concern on social media, with some users questioning the aircraft's altitude and the timing of the stadium's pyrotechnics.“It looks like the airplanes almost hit the top of Cape Town stadium,” one user wrote.Another said, “That was a bit dicey if you ask me. Shoo-wee,” while a third described the manoeuvre as potentially catastrophic.Aviation experts said camera perspective could have contributed to the appearance of the aircraft flying extremely close to the roof. Changes in the aircraft's pitch and viewing angles can also affect how close a flypast appears.Airlink defends approved flypastAirlink said the operation had involved extensive planning and rehearsal because the aircraft were flying at low altitude and around 150 knots, or about 280 kmph.According to the airline, onboard records indicated that both aircraft remained within the speed and altitude parameters approved for the manoeuvre. SACAA has yet to independently confirm the claim.Airlink said six senior captains were assigned to the operation, with three crew members aboard each aircraft covering command, co-pilot and safety and technical duties.The formation featured a green Embraer E190 and a black Embraer E195, representing the colours of the Springboks and All Blacks. The same aircraft had performed a formation flypast over Johannesburg's Ellis Park a week earlier before the opening Test.South African aviation analyst Guy Leitch said the jets had flown lower than necessary but rejected suggestions that the operation was reckless.“They flew an approved sequence, they flew it within limits, and it was not fundamentally dangerous,” he said.However, other aviation experts questioned whether the relatively narrow clearance was appropriate over a crowded stadium. Aviation expert Peter Harbison told 9 News Sydney that the flypast should not have been permitted, according to IOL.Flypast follows famous 1995 precedentStadium flypasts have a long association with South African rugby. One of the most famous examples took place before the 1995 Rugby World Cup final, when a South African Airways Boeing 747 flew over Ellis Park in Johannesburg before South Africa played New Zealand.Saturday's Test saw South Africa beat New Zealand 33-26, levelling the four-match series at 1-1 in front of 56,589 spectators.The teams will meet again in Johannesburg on September 5. Another Airlink flypast is planned for the third Test at FNB Stadium in Soweto, subject to conditions and final approvals.SACAA is now reviewing the aircraft data to determine whether the Cape Town flypast remained within its authorised safety parameters.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Women Commission chairperson Lata Gupta on Monday condemned the gangrape of a 16-year-old girl inside a moving sleeper bus and said those responsible must be punished. “The person behind this must get punishment. Immediate action was taken with the arrest of the bus driver and conductor,” Gupta said while speaking to news agency ANI.Police has subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur and seized the sleeper bus."When a woman is facing any problem, if there is a lack of coordination among the agencies dealing with her case, it is the commission's responsibility to improve that coordination, whether with the courts or the police administration," she told news agency PTI.Teen boarded bus seeking help amid heavy rainThe Class 11 student from Uttar Pradesh was gangraped inside the bus after she boarded it seeking help while stranded in heavy rain, police said. The incident took place on the night of August 4 in Delhi, after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family and set out to meet her cousin in Noida.According to police, the girl mistakenly got off at Pari Chowk amid heavy rain and darkness. An empty sleeper bus passing through the area stopped after she signalled for help. The driver, Kuldeep, and conductor, Sandeep, allegedly told her that the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to board.The bus then travelled nearly 47 kilometres towards Kashmere Gate. The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal late at night and fled.The girl told police that both the driver and conductor raped her and threatened to kill her when she resisted.Bus company says duo were sent for repairsMonu Gupta, manager of the bus travel company that owns the vehicle, said the driver and conductor had been asked to take the bus to Timarpur for repairs. “We had asked the driver and conductor to take the bus to Timarpur for repair. The next morning, we received a call from the Administration; we were told that the bus had been seized and the driver and conductor were arrested,” he said.Gupta said both the driver and conductor were from rural Kanpur and had been working with the company for the past two years. “We have submitted their Aadhaar cards to the Police. They have been working here for the last two years,” he added.The driver and conductor have been arrested in connection with the case, and the bus has been seized as police continue their investigation.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Man arrested after Swiss rave shooting that killed 22-year-old woman
articles.summary: A 22-year-old Italian woman was killed and several injured at a techno rave in Aarau.
articles.body:
A 43-year-old Swiss man has been arrested following a shooting at a rave in Switzerland in which a woman was killed.

Italian 22-year-old Maria Spinelli was killed and several others injured at a techno rave being held at a horse racing track in Aarau, a town about 46km (29 miles) west of Zurich on Sunday.

The shooting initiated a nearly 24-hour manhunt before Aarau cantonal police confirmed they apprehended the suspect shortly before 01:00 local time on Monday (23:00 GMT on Sunday).

"The investigation into the exact sequence of events, the background and the possible motive is currently under way," police said in a statement. "At this time, it is assumed that the perpetrator acted alone."

Police first received a report of shots fired at the Schachen race track at about 02:30 local time on Sunday.

Spinelli died at the scene, while four men and a woman, aged between 24 and 27, were taken to hospital with injuries "ranging from minor to severe".

An eyewitness told Swiss news outlet Blick that he had "suddenly heard the gunshots" minutes after the music stopped, initially believing they were fireworks.

He said he was told to hide by a man and a woman, the latter of whom was shot.

Organisers had expected 3,500 people to attend. Aarau, home to approximately 23,000 people, is less than 40km from the border with Germany, where local media reported police were supporting Swiss forces.

The arrest marks a quick progression in the police investigation - on Sunday afternoon, the force in Aarau said it had no leads on the perpetrator and was unsure whether it was one person or several.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni previously said she was confident Swiss authorities would "shed full light on what happened and find anyone responsible".

Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement that it was sending officials to Zurich "to closely follow the investigation".

Switzerland has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in Europe, although violent shootings are rare and tighter controls were introduced in recent years.

The last major shooting occurred in 2001, when 14 members of the parliament and local government of Zug, near Lucerne, were killed by a gunman who then took his own life.

articles.title: Laurance Rockefeller first saw undeveloped St. John from a boat in 1952; his conservation group later acquired about 5,000 acres and gave them to create a US national park
articles.summary: US News: What if one of America’s most beautiful national parks began with a wealthy conservationist simply looking at an undeveloped island from a boat? In 19.
articles.body: What if one of America’s most beautiful national parks began with a wealthy conservationist simply looking at an undeveloped island from a boat? In 1952, Laurance Rockefeller sailed past St. John in the U.S. Virgin Islands and was struck by its untouched landscape. At the time, the island had no proper roads, cars, electricity or dock, according to the National Park Service. Rockefeller believed the island’s natural beauty was worth preserving before development transformed it. Over the following four years, his conservation organisation, Jackson Hole Preserve, acquired approximately 5,000 acres of St. John and transferred the land to the federal government. That donation became the foundation for Virgin Islands National Park, which Congress established in 1956. The National Park Service credits Rockefeller’s land donation as a major factor in the creation of the park.A chance encounterWhen Rockefeller first approached St. John in 1952, the island was still largely undeveloped. According to the National Park Service, it had no proper roads, cars, electricity or dock. Those conditions made an impression on Rockefeller, who considered St. John one of the most beautiful places he had ever seen. He had also come across a 1939 report exploring the possibility of establishing a national park on the island. Rockefeller was already involved in conservation by this point. The National Park Service describes him as an influential conservationist and philanthropist who played a major role in promoting the preservation of natural areas and expanding opportunities for outdoor recreation. His interest in St. John therefore developed into something more substantial than admiration for the landscape. He began looking for a way to ensure that the island's undeveloped areas could remain protected.Buying land for preservationRockefeller and the nonprofit Jackson Hole Preserve began purchasing property on St. John. Over roughly four years, they acquired approximately 5,000 acres. The land was then transferred to the federal government to help establish a national park. At the time, St. John covered about 12,500 acres, meaning the donated land represented a substantial portion of the island.The National Park Service's historical account documents the connection between Rockefeller's 1952 visit, the subsequent land purchases and the eventual creation of the park. The U.S. Department of the Interior has likewise stated that Virgin Islands National Park was established largely through Rockefeller's initial land donation through Jackson Hole Preserve. Congress formally authorised Virgin Islands National Park on August 2, 1956. The park opened to the public on December 1 that year.The park growsRockefeller's original donation provided the foundation, but the protected area eventually expanded beyond those first 5,000 acres. In 1962, Congress added 5,650 acres of submerged waters surrounding St. John to the park. Additional areas were incorporated over the following decades, including land on Hassel Island in St. Thomas Harbor in 1978.Today according to the National Park Service, Virgin Islands National Park encompasses 7,259 acres of land on St. John, representing more than half of the island. The park protects tropical forests, beaches, coral reefs and other coastal environments, while also preserving historic sites connected to the island's past. The Department of the Interior reported in 2008 that the park encompassed nearly 13,000 acres of land and water within its boundaries. The conservation story continued in 2001 when President Bill Clinton established the Virgin Islands Coral Reef National Monument, protecting thousands of acres of submerged land and marine habitat adjacent to the national park.A lasting legacyRockefeller's contribution to St. John became one of the defining achievements of his long conservation career. He spent decades supporting efforts to protect natural resources, historic places and opportunities for public recreation. In 1991, President George H. W. Bush awarded Rockefeller the Congressional Gold Medal in recognition of his leadership in natural resource conservation and historic preservation.But his connection to St. John remains particularly striking because of how it began. In 1952, Rockefeller encountered an undeveloped island from the water. Within a few years, he and Jackson Hole Preserve had acquired thousands of acres and transferred them to the federal government. That land became the foundation of a national park that continues to protect much of St. John's natural landscape today. What began as a view from a boat ultimately helped ensure that the island's forests, beaches and surrounding waters would remain protected for generations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Italy population to shrink by nearly 4 million by 2050 as ageing accelerates: Report
articles.summary: Europe News: Italy's population is projected to shrink by almost 4 million people by 2050, with a rapidly ageing population posing fresh challenges for the country.
articles.body: Italy's population is projected to shrink by almost 4 million people by 2050, with a rapidly ageing population posing fresh challenges for the country's economy and welfare system, according to new projections released by the national statistics bureau ISTAT on Monday.Italy's resident population is expected to fall to 55 million by 2050, from 58.9 million at the start of 2025, before declining further to 45.8 million by 2080, ISTAT said, according to Reuters.The projections come as Italy continues to grapple with a long-running decline in births and a growing elderly population.Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni had made boosting the birth rate a government priority after taking office in 2022, but births have continued to fall.Births remain near record lowsBirths have declined steadily in Italy since 2008 and fell to around 355,000 last year, the lowest figure since the country's unification in 1861.ISTAT projected that annual births would remain broadly stable until 2030 before falling further to 335,000 by 2050.Deaths, meanwhile, are expected to rise as Italy's large post-war baby boom generation reaches old age. The number of annual deaths is projected to increase from around 652,000 last year to a peak of 869,000 in 2058.Earlier ISTAT data showed that Italy's fertility rate had fallen to an average of 1.14 children per woman, well below the replacement rate of 2.1.Elderly population set to grow sharplyThe share of Italians aged 65 and above is projected to rise to 34.5% in 2050, compared with 24.7% in 2025.At the same time, the proportion of the population of working age, defined as those between 15 and 64 years, is expected to fall to 55.3% from 63.4%.A shrinking pool of workers alongside a growing number of pensioners will pose "new challenges to the economic system and welfare," ISTAT said.Southern Italy faces steepest declineThe demographic decline is expected to vary significantly across the country.Poorer southern Italy is forecast to see the sharpest population losses, with its population falling from 19.7 million in 2025 to 16.7 million by 2050.Central and northern regions are also expected to record population declines, although the projected fall will be more modest.Immigration has helped offset population declineEarlier ISTAT data had shown that Italy's population stabilised after 12 years of decline, with immigration almost entirely offsetting the country's shrinking number of births.As of January 1, Italy's resident population stood at 58.94 million, virtually unchanged from a year earlier.ISTAT had said that without sustained migration inflows, Italy's population would resume shrinking, adding to long-term pressure on the labour market and public finances.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
